Shameless Snacks · creative report · 19 Aug 2026

Whitelisting: what wins

For the video editing team. Built 2026-08-19 from every whitelisting cut that earned money.

How this was built: 156 WL tasks, 11,236 ad-days, $348k spend from the ad database. Pulled the 38 cuts that spent over $800 and returned above 0.55 CM-ROAS, downloaded every one, and watched them frame by frame. Everything below comes from those 38 videos, not from opinion.

How to read CM-ROAS: contribution margin per dollar spent. 1.0 = breakeven. Higher is better. The whole account runs under 1.0 right now, so treat these as a ranking, not a scoreboard.

1. Start here: five things to change tomorrow

  1. Cut to 16 to 25 seconds. That length bucket returns 0.538. The 36 to 50 second bucket returns 0.471 and is where most of our budget went. We have been shipping the wrong length.
  2. Put the product in the top half of the frame, not just in her hand. Same footage, two treatments: SH-17230-2 full frame returned 0.552. SH-17230-7 split screen with product B-roll on top returned 0.844. That is +53% margin from an edit decision alone.
  3. Open on something that is not a face. The strongest openers are product macro, a blowtorch, a product lineup with an offer card, or a title card. Face-first openers underperform.
  4. Hands in frame at all times. Palm of loose gummies, bag pushed at the lens, opening the pack, eating on camera. Every single winner does this. Dead hands equals dead hold rate.
  5. Lead with taste, never with fiber. Our highest scoring cut at scale opens on "if you love a sour candy" and does not mention a single number until second six. Taste promise first, stats as proof after.

2. Length is the biggest lever you control

length cuts spend CM-ROAS
15s or under 37 $11,333 0.475
16 to 25s 140 $64,717 0.538
26 to 35s 152 $49,875 0.483
36 to 50s 127 $108,857 0.471
51 to 90s 51 $18,538 0.423

Under 15s is too short to land the taste promise plus one proof point. Over 35s is where people leave. Target 16 to 25 seconds. If the raw footage will not compress that far, cut two shorter pieces instead of one long one.

One exception: the two 144 second cuts (SH-13646-1 at 0.609, SH-15585-1 at 0.747) work as long-form qualifiers even though under 1% of viewers finish. Do not treat that as permission to run long by default. It is a separate format, deliberately chosen, not a failure to trim.

3. The six hooks that earned

A. Offer card cold open

SH-13647-5 StephJoplin, $11,692, 0.820. Highest earner at real scale. Three seconds of product lineup B-roll with a bold offer card over it. The creator does not speak until second four. Then she comes in mid-thought with "I just crushed one of these." Build it: static or slow-push product lineup, bold offer card centered, urgency line, hard cut to creator mid-sentence.

▶ Watch SH-13647-5 in Air

B. Comedy sketch with a second person

SH-10846-6 BizValentini, $1,137, 1.334. The only cut in the entire whitelisting library above breakeven. Title sticker: "How To Eat Your Snacks Without Sharing." A second person's hand reaches in from off frame and steals a gummy. "WAIT. You have your own. I'm taking one. Well then you owe me one." Build it: it is a bit, not an ad. If the raw has any moment of a partner, kid, or friend stealing food, that is your opener. This is the highest-return device we have and we have used it once.

▶ Open SH-10846-6 board in Air

C. Taste conditional

SH-16302-8 JanssenBradshaw, $3,043, 0.911. "If you love a sour candy, you should 100% try these." Then 70 calories per bag, then 26 grams of fiber, then the flavor tour. Build it: taste promise first, stats second, always in that order.

▶ Watch SH-16302-8 in Air

D. Disbelief / rhetorical challenge

SH-14904-4 AshleyZeffiro, $1,382, 0.715. "You're telling me I can eat a bag of candy and get 26 grams of fiber?" Build it: state the objection as disbelief in the creator's own voice, then answer it with the palm-of-gummies shot.

▶ Watch SH-14904-4 in Air

E. Relatable scene title card

SH-15609-3 AshleyPeeta, $2,035, 0.556. Opens on a card: "Me immediately after dropping the kids at school." No claim, no product, just a moment people recognise. Build it: "Me when / Me immediately after / POV" plus an everyday moment. Rotate the moment. Do not reuse the same scene twice in a sprint.

▶ Watch SH-15609-3 in Air

F. Self-deprecating confession

SH-16200-4 JessicaDeJohn, $4,270, 0.620, 49% hook rate, the highest in the set. "I don't know about you but I used to get them in bulk. Like the shovel, if you're a civilized person. But I'd just grab them by the handful." Build it: creator admits a slightly embarrassing habit before mentioning the product. Highest scroll stop of anything we have made.

Also proven: the comment reply sticker. SH-12873-4 AmyMain at 0.773 and SH-15101-5 PhilCowley at 0.933 both open with a native "Reply to [user]'s comment" sticker. It works because it looks like organic content, not an ad. Keep the sticker device and write a fresh comment over it.

▶ Watch SH-12873-4 in Air  ·  Watch SH-15101-5 in Air

▶ Watch SH-16200-4 in Air

4. The five compositions that earned

1. Split screen, product on top. SH-17230-7, 0.844. Top half is product B-roll for the entire runtime (box, bags laid on grass, gummies dropping into a glass jar). Bottom half is the talking head. Product is never off screen. Same footage full frame scored 0.552. This is the most transferable win in the report and only one creator has ever received it.

▶ Watch SH-17230-7 in Air

2. Product spread in the foreground. SH-16300-1 CassandraGarcia, SH-17215-2 LauraFlusche. Six or more bags fanned across the counter in the bottom third of frame for the whole video. The creator is behind them. Frame always sells even when she is just talking.

▶ Watch SH-16300-1 in Air  ·  Watch SH-17215-2 in Air

3. Authority set dressing. SH-16360 and SH-15101 PhilCowley. White coat, pharmacy shelves behind him. The background does the credentialing so nothing has to be claimed out loud. If a creator has a real setting that implies expertise, shoot it there and keep it in frame.

4. Second character in frame. SH-16384-1 (husband being fed in the car, 0.763), SH-17215-2 (kid reaching for the bag), SH-10846-6 (hand stealing a gummy, 1.334). Three of our best cuts. A second person converts a monologue into a scene.

▶ Watch SH-16384-1 in Air  ·  Watch SH-17215-2 in Air  ·  Open SH-10846-6 board in Air

5. Hands and mouth. Every winner. Palm of loose gummies held to lens, bag torn open on camera, gummy eaten and reacted to. SH-13647-5 does all three inside 46 seconds. If you have twenty seconds of talking head with no hands, you have twenty seconds of nothing.

▶ Watch SH-13647-5 in Air

5. Captions and motion graphics

Two caption systems both work. Pick one per cut and stay consistent.

System A, high energy. All caps, one to three words per card, keyword highlighted in a second colour (yellow on white is our most used). Used on SH-16360-1, SH-13647-5, SH-16300-1. Fits pharmacist, high energy, fast cut pieces.

System B, lifestyle. Lowercase sentence fragments, keyword in solid white and filler words in grey so the eye lands on the word that matters. Used on SH-16200-4, SH-15585-1, SH-15609-3. Fits car selfie and kitchen pieces.

Devices worth stealing: - Stat checkmarks. SH-16376-7: a yellow tick animates in under each number as she says it. Three grams of sugar, tick. 70 calories, tick. 26 grams of fiber, tick. - Stat chips. SH-13883-7: green chip for "70 calories", red banner for "LOTS OF FIBER". - Red arrow pointer. SH-13293-1: animated arrow pointing at the bag in hand. - Emoji stickers as punctuation. Raspberry, fire, shocked face. Used on the 0.911 and the 0.604 cuts. It is a house template, not a creator quirk. Keep using it. - Whip or tumble transition. SH-16376-7 uses a spinning frame between beats to reset attention at the halfway mark.

Do not: stack four lines of static text on screen and hold it for ten seconds (SH-16302-1 does this and is the weakest of its family at 0.646 versus 0.911 for the sibling).

6. Talking points that earn

Keep these. They appear again and again in the top cuts:

  • Taste first: "these legitimately taste like your favourite candy", "they actually do taste like candy", "I'm obsessed"
  • Bare stats: 26g fiber, 70 calories, 3g sugar, 3g net carbs
  • Broccoli comparison: more fiber than three cups of broccoli
  • Flavor tour: name each SKU by its marketing name while holding the bag to the lens. Berry Cherry, Super Sour Blue Raspberry, Green Apple Blast, Wassup Watermelon, OMG Peach
  • Occasions: movie night, the car, the school run, the plane, keeping a bag in the pantry, in my purse
  • Sweet-tooth language: "scratch the sweet", "calm the sugar craving", "non guilty pleasure"

7. How to use this across a batch of five

This is not a gate every cut has to pass. It is the shape most of the batch should take.

Three of five: run the default pattern. These are the settings we know return money. Use them unless you have a reason not to.

  • 16 to 25 seconds
  • First two seconds are not a talking head
  • Product visible in the first frame and never off screen for more than two seconds
  • Hands doing something in every shot
  • Taste mentioned before fiber
  • One caption system, used consistently
  • At least one device from section 5

Two of five: swing. Break something on purpose. The batch is where we find the next pattern, and it will not come from five cuts that all obey the same rules.

Two facts worth sitting with:

  • SH-16200-4 has the highest hook rate we have ever recorded at 49%, and it opens on a talking head. It breaks the second rule on this page.
  • SH-10846-6 is the only cut above breakeven at 1.334, and it leads with a joke rather than the taste promise. It breaks the fifth.

If either editor had been held to the checklist, neither would exist.

What a good swing looks like: a different opening device, a format we have not tried on this creator, a comedy premise, a second character, an unusual composition, a length outside the range because the idea genuinely needs it. Something you can name in one sentence when you hand it over.

What a swing is not: the default pattern executed loosely. Same structure, no hook, hands out of frame, product missing for eight seconds. That is not exploration, that is a cut that got away from you. If you cannot say what you were testing, it belongs in the three.

One rule that does not bend: the five cuts in a batch must not open the same way as each other. Five variations of one opener teaches us nothing, and the buyer kills four of them inside a fortnight anyway.
